why: The doc sentence is verbatim (sub-agents.md:893, section 'Session subagent limit'; whole line adds the env var, 'no upper bound, but the limit can't be turned off', and 'Requires Claude Code v2.1.212 or later'). The cited repo lines are also accurate as far as they go: packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:49 does describe maxAgents (default 1000) as 'maximum agent() calls per workflow run', and packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1497 does pass getMaxAgents into createWorkflowTool. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, and the word 'solely' is the error. maxAgents has a SECOND consumer the name-based grep never reached: packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1280 passes it into the shared spawner as maxFanout (configureSpawnerForGeneration), and packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:603 stamps it onto EVERY spawn's budgets as 'fanout: cfg.maxFanout ?? 100'. configureSpawner is the single spawner used by the subagent tool, forks, the review tool and workflow agents alike (index.ts:131,1274,1803,1883). The host then enforces it cumulatively per session at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 - 'if (children.length >= input.budgets.fanout) throw new Error("child-session-fanout-limit")' - where 'children' is the persisted, UNFILTERED record list for this parentSessionKey; the status filter on the adjacent line is the separate concurrency check. So a finished subagent still counts, exactly like Claude's session limit. packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.test.ts:178-183 proves it: after child-1 is stopped, a start with fanout:1 rejects with child-session-fanout-limit. Default is 1000 (DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG.maxAgents, packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:109), plumbed through the init contract (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:314). The claimed evidence grep is true but proves only that Claude's NAMES are absent, not that the mechanism is: this repo spells it fanout/maxAgents, which is the exact 'identifier looks unwired, consequence is false because another layer already handles it' trap AGENTS.md warns about. 'No per-session subagent counter or cap exists anywhere' and 'A session can spawn subagents without bound' are both false. Not an inert-worklist owner decision and not a de-brand difference - just a wrong reading.
correctedState: A cumulative per-session subagent cap DOES exist, under different names. orchestrator.maxAgents (default 1000, packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:109) reaches the shared spawner as maxFanout (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1280) and rides on every spawn as budgets.fanout (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:603), for subagents, forks, review and workflow agents alike. The host enforces it at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 by counting ALL child records for the parent session, terminal ones included, and throws 'child-session-fanout-limit' when the count reaches the budget. Two real but much narrower divergences remain: (1) naming and defaults - 1000 rather than 200, no CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION env var (it is set through orchestrator config), and the error is 'child-session-fanout-limit' rather than 'Subagent spawn limit reached' with the doc's 'do the rest yourself' guidance; (2) accounting shape - each session node keeps its own counter, clamped downward on inheritance via Math.min at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:11142, whereas Claude charges nested subagents, forks and background subagents to one session-wide budget. Also note the sibling limits already match in kind: orchestrator.concurrency (16) is checked on the adjacent line 149 as the concurrent-subagent analogue, and orchestrator.depth is the depth limit.
